sourcedFrom: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:TC_IMPACT_063011, P/N 00084003 (2011)
cleanIntro: The T/C Impact! is a break-action inline muzzleloader with a threaded breech plug carrying Triple-Lead threads. Everything below is Thompson/Center's own published procedure for this rifle, quoted from its manual. Nothing here is a routine for a different T/C model — the Impact's plug does not interchange with any other one they make.

steps.title: Confirm the rifle is unprimed and uncharged
steps.action: Before touching anything else, establish that there is no primer in the breech plug and no charge in the barrel. A muzzleloader gives you no extractor and no ejection port to check through, so this is the only verification you get.
steps.caution: Never clean or disassemble a charged or primed muzzleloader.
steps.quote: Make sure that the firearm is unprimed and uncharged.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:TC_IMPACT_063011, P/N 00084003 — Disassembly of the T/C Impact Muzzleloading Rifle — p.37

steps.title: Sight through the ignition fire channel
steps.action: Hold the muzzle up to a light source and look down the ignition fire channel from the breech end. Seeing daylight is what proves the bore is empty; if the channel is dark, treat the rifle as charged and stop.
steps.quote: Make sure there is no primer seated. Next, holding the muzzle up to the light, look through the ignition fire channel to make sure you can see through it. If you can not see through it, it is charged or the channel is obstructed and it will be necessary for you to remove the breech plug.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:TC_IMPACT_063011, P/N 00084003 — Disassembly of the T/C Impact Muzzleloading Rifle — p.37
steps.warn: A dark channel means charged OR obstructed. Both are stop conditions.

steps.title: If it is charged, pull the charge before going further
steps.action: With the action open and the rifle confirmed unprimed, take the breech plug out and let gravity do the work. The powder drops out of the breech end first, and only then does the bullet get pushed clear.
steps.aside: To push the bullet fully out, the manual has you add the extended jag that came with the rifle to your ramrod, or use a longer range rod.
steps.quote: Once the breech plug has been removed, point the muzzle up. Gravity should then cause the pellets or the loose powder to drop out. The bullet can then be poked out of the bore with your ramrod.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:TC_IMPACT_063011, P/N 00084003 — Unloading a Charge from the T/C Impact — p.30

steps.title: Remove the ramrod
steps.action: Draw the ramrod out of the thimbles under the barrel and put it somewhere it will not roll off the bench — you need it again for the bore work.
steps.quote: Remove the ramrod from the thimble(s) and set it aside.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:TC_IMPACT_063011, P/N 00084003 — Disassembly of the T/C Impact Muzzleloading Rifle — p.37

steps.title: Open the action at the hood ears
steps.action: Pull rearward on the hood ears and tip the barrel down. This is the Impact's own opening motion — it is not a trigger-guard lever like the swing-block T/C rifles, and the breech plug comes into view as the barrel drops.
steps.quote: Open the action by pulling rearward on the hood ears and tipping the barrel down. This will expose the breech plug.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:TC_IMPACT_063011, P/N 00084003 — Disassembly of the T/C Impact Muzzleloading Rifle — p.37

steps.title: Unscrew the breech plug
steps.action: Fit the supplied wrench and turn counter-clockwise as seen from the breech end. Expect it to resist at first — that is the gas seal letting go, and it is normal. If the barrel turns in your hand instead, hold the barrel lug in a vise or a crescent wrench.
steps.caution: The Impact plug is not interchangeable with any other T/C muzzleloader. Check for the identifier groove before you put one back in.
steps.quote: Insert the breech plug wrench onto the breech plug. Turn counter-clockwise to unscrew the breech plug. You may have to exert some initial force in order to “break” the gas seal, which formed when the breech plug was originally “snugged” to the barrel during installation.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:TC_IMPACT_063011, P/N 00084003 — Disassembly of the T/C Impact Muzzleloading Rifle — p.37

steps.title: Know which plug belongs in this rifle
steps.action: The Impact's plug has Triple-Lead threads and an identifier groove. A single-lead plug from another T/C model can look near enough to fool you across the bench, and it must not go in.
steps.quote: The IMPACT Breech Plug has Triple-Lead threads which provide for quick removal from the firearm and improved ease of release when fouled. This breech plug DOES NOT interchange with any other model of T/C muzzleloader.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:TC_IMPACT_063011, P/N 00084003 — Thorough Cleaning — p.36
steps.warn: Improper type or installation of breech plugs can cause injury and damage to property.

steps.title: Scrub the bore with the supplied jag
steps.action: Thread the jag that came with the rifle onto the ramrod, wrap a patch soaked in black-powder solvent over it, and work it the length of the bore several times until the patches stop coming out grey.
steps.prose: Black powder and its substitutes leave a residue that is actively corrosive, not merely dirty. Follow the wet patches with dry ones until the bore is dry.
steps.quote: Use the cleaning jag that was provided with the T/C IMPACT, and a cleaning patch saturated with a bore cleaner like Thompson/Center’s Number 13® Bore Cleaner. Run the saturated patch up and down the bore a few times - to remove the fouling
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:TC_IMPACT_063011, P/N 00084003 — Field Cleaning — p.33

steps.title: Clean and oil the breech assembly
steps.action: Take a soft bristle brush dampened with solvent to the breech assembly, get it dry, then put a light film of oil on it. Follow with moisture-displacing oil into the firing pin.
steps.quote: Clean the breech assembly with a soft bristle brush dampened with some solvent. When the breech assembly is dry, lightly oil it.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:TC_IMPACT_063011, P/N 00084003 — Field Cleaning — p.33

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The barrel is clear, the breech plug is out and clean, and the bore and breech assembly are serviced. That is as far as routine maintenance goes on the Impact. Going deeper — forend, stock and hood assembly — is the manual's own disassembly section and is covered in the Deep Clean.
steps.quote: If the IMPACT muzzleloader has become very dirty due to extensive firing, the shooter may need to disassemble the rifle further than just removing the breech plug.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:TC_IMPACT_063011, P/N 00084003 — Thorough Cleaning — p.36

deepSteps.title: Scrub the plug and both sets of threads
deepSteps.action: With the plug out, clean the fouling off it and get a stiff brush and solvent into the barrel's internal threads as well. Both sides get dried, then anti-seize — this is what stops the plug seizing in place next season.
deepSteps.quote: Once removed, the breech plug should be scrubbed free of fouling and then the threads should be lubricated with an anti-seize lubricant like T/C's Super Lube, before reinstallation. The threads inside the breech end of the barrel must also be cleaned thoroughly with a stiff brush and solvent and then dried and lubricated with anti-seize lubricant.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:TC_IMPACT_063011, P/N 00084003 — Thorough Cleaning — p.35

deepSteps.title: Flush the barrel with hot soapy water
deepSteps.action: Stand the muzzle in a pan of hot soapy water and pump a wet patch on the jag up and down from the breech end. The barrel acts as its own pump and draws the water through, carrying the fouling out with it.
deepSteps.caution: Dry it completely before oiling. Water left in a black-powder bore rusts it fast.
deepSteps.quote: Pump the ramrod and patch up and down in the barrel. This will draw water into the barrel and flush out the fouling. When the barrel is clean, wipe off any excess water and allow it to dry.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:TC_IMPACT_063011, P/N 00084003 — Thorough Cleaning — p.35

deepSteps.title: Take the forend off
deepSteps.action: Two screws hold the forend to the barrel. Back them out and lift the forend clear.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the forend by unscrewing the two forend screws (#3 in FIGURE 30).
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:TC_IMPACT_063011, P/N 00084003 — Disassembly — p.38

deepSteps.title: Lift the barreled action out of the stock
deepSteps.action: Two bolts hold the stock to the barreled action — one takes a 3/16 inch Allen wrench, the other 5/32 inch. With both out, the barreled action lifts up and forward. Watch for the hood spring: it lives loose in a hole in the stock and it is easy to lose.
deepSteps.aside: The manual notes the hood spring resides in a hole in the stock and should be removed and cleaned during this procedure.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the two bolts that hold the stock to the barreled action (Items #1 & #2 in FIGURE 31). Then lift the barreled action up and forward - out of the stock.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:TC_IMPACT_063011, P/N 00084003 — Disassembly — p.38

deepSteps.title: Drift the hood retaining pin and lift the hood
deepSteps.action: Push the hood retaining pin out with a 1/8 inch drift, then lift the hood assembly straight up off the breech block. This is the deepest the manual takes the Impact.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the hood retaining pin (#5 in FIGURE 31) with a 1/8˝ drift (punch).
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:TC_IMPACT_063011, P/N 00084003 — Disassembly — p.39
deepSteps.warn: Never disassemble the rifle beyond the procedures outlined in the manual.

deepSteps.title: Clean the stripped parts, then reverse the order
deepSteps.action: Solvent every part, dry them, and put a light film of oil on the metal. Reassembly is the same sequence backwards, and it ends with a function check before the rifle sees a charge again.
deepSteps.quote: Clean all parts with an appropriate cleaning solvent. Dry the parts and lightly lubricate the metal surfaces to prevent rust and corrosion.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:TC_IMPACT_063011, P/N 00084003 — Disassembly — p.39

deepSteps.title: Seat the breech plug to snug — and know what snug means
deepSteps.action: Thread the plug in clockwise with the wrench, carefully, feeling that the threads have picked up straight. T/C defines the endpoint by feel rather than by torque, and the definition is precise enough to work with.
deepSteps.caution: Be certain the threads are not cross-threaded before you apply any force.
deepSteps.quote: “Snug” is defined as being as tight as you can turn it into the barrel by using the supplied breech plug wrench and turning it clockwise, while holding the barrel in your hand. When you can no longer grip the barrel, and it turns in your hand, the breech plug is “snug”.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:TC_IMPACT_063011, P/N 00084003 — Disassembly — p.39

cleaning.name: Bore and breech
tasks: Run solvent-soaked patches on the supplied jag up and down the bore until they come out clean
Follow with dry patches until the bore is dry
Brush the breech assembly with a soft bristle brush dampened with solvent, dry it, then oil it lightly
Work moisture-displacing oil into the firing pin within the breech

cleaning.name: Breech plug
tasks: Scrub all fouling off the plug
Clean the barrel's internal breech threads with a stiff brush and solvent, then dry them
Lubricate both the plug threads and the barrel threads with anti-seize
Confirm the plug carries the Impact identifier groove before reinstalling

cleaning.name: Exterior
tasks: Avoid heavy grease or oil — in cold weather it can congeal and slow the hammer fall

reassembly: Lubricate the plug threads and the barrel's breech threads with anti-seize
Thread the breech plug in clockwise with the wrench until snug, checking the threads are not cross-threaded
If stripped further: fit the hood assembly to the breech block and drive the hood retaining pin home
Seat the hood spring in its hole in the stock
Lower the barreled action into the stock and fit both stock bolts
Fit the forend with its two screws
Return the ramrod to the thimbles
fncheck: With the rifle unprimed and uncharged, check the sliding hood and the trigger/hammer mechanism for proper function before loading and firing. The manual requires this after any disassembly: check for proper functioning of the barrel and the hammer/trigger mechanism prior to loading and firing.
